claims.text: Tiles: band E (atlas x1580-1760, y1376-1664 = 180x288 px, about 50.6 z7 hexes; 45 whole hex cells cx50-54 x cy43-51 plus a 20 px strip of cx49) lies in exactly six z5 tiles, x 12..13 by y 10..12 (tiles/5/<x>/<y>.jpg, 256x256 jpg, 128 atlas px per tile, 2 tile px per atlas px; the band is 360x576 tile px). All six files exist. The band sits wholly inside the DEM window 1060,1240,1860,2040, so R22 allows relief here, but the print carries none.

Inventory of what the print draws in band E (nothing else): a black wavy coastline stroke with a headland, a bay and a hooked inlet; one flat grey-olive sea; three ring-dot settlements with bold slab-serif labels (Tamaron double-ring, Mago and Perona single-ring); one dotted black road network; one two-line spaced-capital region lettering (AURA-HOTH- / HANATH); three letters of a spaced italic sea name (R, E, A); and one thin dark-grey graticule line across the top. Ink (luminance <110) is 5.7% of band pixels (11,735 of 207,360). No river, no island, no peak, no height numeral, no wash, no trail.

claims.text: Settlement class: three ring glyphs, all with a bold slab-serif label. Tamaron is a double ring (outer ring about 10.5x11.5 atlas px with a heavy inner dot), centre 1658.8,1554.1, label above it centred on the ring (label ink x1626-1689, y1534-1544, about 10 px tall). Mago is a single ring (outer 8 atlas px), centre 1689.7,1582.8, label to its upper right (x1691-1728, y1564-1577). Perona is a single ring (8 px), centre 1647.8,1631.8, label below it (x1622-1672, y1637-1648, with a macron on the o). All three labels are fully legible. Ring-to-ring gaps: Tamaron-Mago 42 px, Tamaron-Perona 78 px, Mago-Perona 65 px, so no knot or cluster. The double ring marks the major-city class (Magosh-class glyph, CLAUDE.md key), so band E holds the one double-ring city of the Leponnia coast east of Epeshu.

claims.text: Road class: the print draws black round dots (about 2-2.5 atlas px across, pitch about 3.9 px), no colour and no casing; canon key: dotted = major roadways. Resolved dots in band: 57 (about 211 atlas px of visible chain). Runs: (a) west trunk, 16 dots from 1583,1559 to 1634,1580.5 (the chain enters from Rhup); (b) a 4-dot spur leaving the Tamaron ring south, 1657,1563 to 1654,1573; (c) a Tamaron-to-Mago chain of 8 dots, 1666,1558 to 1682,1580; (d) Mago south-east, 7 dots from 1692.5,1588 to 1705.7,1602; (e) a south-east trunk of 22 dots from 1699.5,1612 through 1709,1637 to the east edge at about 1759,1660. The trunk is not drawn between about 1634,1580 and 1699,1612: there the AURA-HOTH-/HANATH lettering sits on its line and the spur and the west trunk both stop at the lettering, so a join under the lettering (about 65-75 px) is inferred, not seen. Total major road in band is about 280 atlas px counting that hidden stretch.

claims.text: Sea, coast and shore shape: the sea fills the north and east of the band as a flat grey-olive field (mean RGB 175,167,127; R stdev 3.3), no depth shading, no wave marks. By flood-fill with a 2 px ink halo the sea is 138,560 of 207,360 band px (66.8%), bare land 41,660 (20.1%), ink and halo 27,140 (13.1%) (an estimate). The coast stroke (about 2 atlas px wide) enters the west edge at y about 1530 and leaves near the east edge at y about 1656 (the road dots reach the edge at 1660). Shore features: a bay west of Tamaron dipping to y about 1567 at x1620; the Tamaron headland tip at about 1659,1548; a small hooked inlet east of Mago at about 1710-1728,1585-1600; then a steady south-east run (coast y about 1632 at x1720, 1647 at x1740). There is no island in the band (the only sea-coloured pockets are letter interiors). Plate one by contrast is a flat light blue sea with no coast stroke.

claims.text: Spaced lettering, two classes plate one lacks. (1) Region name AURA-HOTH- over HANATH: two parallel lines of bold slab capitals about 9 tile px tall (about 4.5 atlas px cap height), set along a south-east bearing of about 41 degrees, from about 1631,1568 (A of AURA) to about 1700,1628 (final hyphen of HOTH-); HANATH runs about 1633,1583 to 1682,1626. It is Aura-hoth-Hanath, one of six regions the wiki Leponnia page lists (Peshunor, Lamor, Aura-hoth-Hanath, Dranimos, Rhoshkhon, Paerandas); the print breaks it over two lines with hyphens. (2) Sea name letters in light italic capitals about 29x26 atlas px: R at about 1588,1404 (clipped by the west edge, x1580-1598), E at 1670,1440 (x1656-1684, y1427-1453), A at about 1752+,1465 (clipped by the east edge, x1744-1760, y1457-1474), pitch about 90 px on a bearing of about 24 degrees. On the wide mosaic the same arc reads G R E A T C H, so these are the GREAT of the sea name (Great Chasmous Sea).

claims.text: Graticule: one thin dark-grey line (mean luminance 80 against about 25-30 for coast, road and letters, so lighter and thinner than any other ink) crosses the top of the band as a smooth arc, entering the top edge at about x1600 and leaving the east edge at about y1399 (about 155 atlas px in band; 1,023 ink px; y about 1379.5 at x1630, 1387.5 at x1680, 1394.9 at x1730). On the wide mosaic it is one of a curved parallel and near-vertical meridians that span the whole sheet, so it is a latitude parallel. Plate one has no graticule (q01-c01), so this is a print class beyond plate one; it is also the only ink in hex F08.

Aura-hoth-Hanath occurs once, in the Leponnia Regions line, with no description. gaps: The hidden stretch of the dotted trunk under the AURA-HOTH-/HANATH lettering (about 65-75 px between 1634,1580 and 1699,1612) is inferred from the dots that stop at the lettering and resume after it; the road's actual course under the letters is not established.

That the R, E, A letters are the GREAT of Great Chasmous Sea is read from the visible G-R-E-A-T-C-H arc on the wide mosaic; the full lettering (S, E and A of the sea name) was not read, and no marker sits on the arc, so the mapping of this lettering to the Great Chasmous Sea marker at 1940.8,1505.4 is inferred.
The thin grey arc is called a graticule from its continuation across the wide mosaic with near-vertical companions; the print has no legend, so the class name is an interpretation.

The 57-dot count and the 280 px road length are estimates: dots touching the coast or letters merge into larger ink components and are not counted; per-dot positions were not fitted to a spline. Sea/land/halo shares use colour thresholds on JPEG tiles (halo around ink is its own bucket), so they are estimates, not polygon areas.
Plate-one class tally uses the 13-class list assembled here from q01-c19; q06 states a different split (4 appear, 9 missing), so the band-by-band class totals need reconciling in synthesis.
Whether plate-one density maps onto this band at any scale is not derivable here (q01 gap: plate-one ground extent is unstated), so no names-per-hex target is set for band E.
Relief for this band comes only from EPESHU_HF, which this question did not read; the print carries no height, so any ridge name or height here must come from the DEM bake or be invented.

Whether the Tamaron marker's drawn glyph at maps-site/index.html:1227 duplicates or replaces the printed double ring at z5-z8 was not rendered or checked; only the code path and the 1.9 px coordinate agreement were read.

Rhup's 'p' descender and a ring-like fragment at the west edge (x1580-1584, y1548-1554) were not separated from the coast stroke, so the exact west-edge coast crossing (about 1530) and the count of ink components at the edge are approximate.
summary: Band E's print draws only a black coast with a headland, bay and inlet, a flat grey-olive sea, three ring-dot cities (Tamaron the double-ring Magosh with 3 anchors/1 marker agreeing), a 57-dot black dotted road network, the AURA-HOTH-/HANATH region lettering, three letters of the GREAT sea name and a graticule arc; of 13 plate-one classes only 3 appear (in another dress) and 10 are missing, including every river, peak, height, wash, trail and relief mark. The data agrees with the print only for the three city-anchors and the Tamaron marker, while the Sun Road trace is a chord (21% of it on printed dots), traced-roads polyline 33 is a mis-trace of the Tamaron and Mago label text, two invented sea lanes end on label text, no wiki page has coordinates, and 16 of 45 whole hexes (15 sea, 1 bare land) are blank, including fixtures F08 (sea plus graticule only) and F01 (bare land plus a Perona ring edge).
